items.headline: Man, 24, dies after being struck by lightning while paddleboarding off Pasir Ris Beach
items.summary: A 24-year-old man died and six others aged 13 to 54 were taken to hospital after a lightning strike hit their group as they kayaked and paddleboarded off Pasir Ris Beach at about 4:50pm on 5 July. Police said there was no sign of foul play and investigations are ongoing.

items.headline: TikTok confirms Singapore layoffs as it restructures its Trust and Safety operations
items.summary: TikTok cut jobs in Singapore on 1 July as part of a global reorganisation of its Trust and Safety (content moderation) division, with one affected worker estimating about 20 people on their team were let go. The company also confirmed layoffs in Indonesia and is reviewing about 300 roles at its Dublin hub.

items.headline: Youth jailed 23 months for soliciting nude images from two underage girls he met online
items.summary: A man who committed the offences while under 18 was sentenced to 23 months' jail and a S$2,000 fine after pleading guilty on 3 July to five of 18 charges, including sexual assault. He cannot be named under a Children and Young Persons Act gag order.

items.headline: Two men arrested after a knife fight outside an Orchard nightclub leaves four injured
items.summary: Four men were injured, one with a neck wound from a knife, in a pre-dawn brawl along Buyong Road near Orchard on 2 July that began inside a nearby nightclub. Police arrested two men, aged 25 and 27, for voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous means and seized a knife.

items.summary: Today's edition could not include India stories: all six allowed India outlets (The Hindu, The Indian Express, Hindustan Times, The Times of India, NDTV, The Economic Times) were unreachable from the compute environment after repeated retry attempts. Normal coverage resumes tomorrow.

items.headline: UK coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: Today's edition could not include UK News stories: both allowed UK outlets (BBC and Sky News) were unreachable from the compute environment after repeated retry attempts. Normal coverage resumes tomorrow.

items.headline: Hamas dissolves the committee that governed Gaza, ceding civilian rule to a technocratic body
items.summary: Hamas announced the dissolution of the Government Emergency Committee that has run Gaza, with its head Mohammed al-Farra resigning, to hand day-to-day governance to a UN-backed Palestinian technocratic committee (NCAG) led by Ali Shaath. It is Hamas's first formal ceding of civilian control since it seized Gaza in 2007.

items.headline: China test-fires a submarine-launched ballistic missile into the Pacific, drawing regional protests
items.summary: China's navy launched a ballistic missile carrying a dummy warhead from a submarine into the South Pacific on Monday, its first publicly acknowledged such test, landing inside the South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone. Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong called it “destabilising”, while Japan and New Zealand also objected.

items.headline: Super Typhoon Bavi makes landfall on the US island of Rota as a Category 5 storm
items.summary: Super Typhoon Bavi struck Rota in the Northern Mariana Islands on Monday morning with winds of about 180mph (290km/h), prompting reports of “major damage”, flash floods and flipped cars. Forecasters warned of up to 20 inches of rain across Guam and the Marianas.

items.headline: FIFA suspends Balogun's red-card ban after a Trump call, prompting protests from UEFA and Belgium
items.summary: FIFA suspended the automatic one-match ban on USA striker Folarin Balogun, freeing him to face Belgium in the World Cup last 16, after President Trump phoned FIFA president Gianni Infantino to ask for a review. UEFA said the move “crossed a red line”; it would be the first World Cup red card since 1962 not to bring a suspension.

items.headline: Israeli drone strike kills at least four in south Lebanon despite a two-week-old ceasefire
items.summary: An Israeli drone struck a car in Nabatieh al-Fawqa in southern Lebanon on 6 July, killing at least four people, including a school principal and her mother. Israel says it targets Hezbollah; the strike tests the US-brokered ceasefire signed on 26 June.

items.headline: Broadcom extends its custom-chip partnership with Apple through 2031
items.summary: Broadcom disclosed a multi-year deal to keep supplying Apple with custom ASIC, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and radio-frequency chips across multiple product generations through 2031, easing fears that Apple would quickly move fully in-house. Apple accounts for roughly 20% of Broadcom's annual revenue; its shares rose more than 3% on Monday.

items.headline: Paris hub Station F reopens its F/ai accelerator after its first AI cohort raised $34 million
items.summary: Xavier Niel's Station F will start a second batch of its F/ai accelerator in September, after its debut cohort of 20 startups raised $34 million in pre-seed funding. Backers include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and AWS; 80% of the founders were repeat entrepreneurs.

items.headline: Nearly 90 startups have reached unicorn status in 2026, most of them AI companies
items.summary: TechCrunch's running tally counts almost 90 new unicorns minted so far in 2026, the majority AI. The list includes Jeff Bezos's Prometheus, valued at $41 billion after a $12 billion round led by JPMorgan and BlackRock, and AI-workspace app Genspark at $2.6 billion.

items.headline: Microsoft cuts 4,800 jobs and will spin off four gaming studios in an Xbox overhaul
items.summary: Microsoft is eliminating about 4,800 roles, or 2.1% of staff, including 1,600 in Xbox, and will spin off studios Compulsion Games, Double Fine, Ninja Theory and Undead Labs as it funds its AI push. Xbox chief Asha Sharma told staff “our business today is not healthy”.

items.headline: The Dow closes above 53,000 for the first time in a chip-led post-holiday rally
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.29% to a record 53,056 on Monday as US markets reopened after the July 4 weekend, with the Nasdaq up 1.1% on a semiconductor rebound. The S&P 500 gained 0.72% to 7,537.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia makes its biggest crude price cut in over two decades as supply swells
items.summary: Saudi Aramco set its flagship Arab Light price to Asia at $1.50 a barrel below the Oman/Dubai benchmark for August, an $11 swing and the largest cut in Reuters records dating to 2003, its first discount since the 2020 price war. It coincided with a fifth straight OPEC+ output hike of 188,000 bpd.

items.headline: SpaceX joins the Nasdaq-100, forcing billions in passive-fund buying
items.summary: SpaceX entered the Nasdaq-100 before Tuesday's open, just 15 trading days after its record June IPO, under the index's new fast-track rule. Funds tracking the benchmark are expected to buy roughly $4.3 billion of the stock, which carries about a 1% weighting.

items.headline: 🎾 Djokovic beats Safiullin for a record 106th Wimbledon win and a place in the quarter-finals
items.summary: Novak Djokovic defeated Roman Safiullin 7-6(4), 6-3, 3-6, 6-3 to reach the Wimbledon quarter-finals and record his 106th singles win at the Championships, moving past Roger Federer's all-time men's record of 105. It is Djokovic's ninth consecutive Wimbledon quarter-final.

items.headline: 🎾 Struff, 36, becomes the oldest man in the Open Era to reach a first Grand Slam quarter-final
items.summary: Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff reached his maiden major quarter-final after Hubert Hurkacz retired in the fifth set of their Wimbledon fourth-round match, with Struff leading 3-6, 6-7(5), 7-6(2), 7-5, 4-2. He next faces defending champion Jannik Sinner.

items.headline: 🏏 India, trailing 1-0, face England in the third T20I at Trent Bridge
items.summary: India, beaten by four wickets in Manchester, look to avoid a series deficit against England in the third of five T20Is at Trent Bridge on 7 July. New captain Shreyas Iyer's side has lost three of its last four completed T20Is.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli's title lead narrows after a Silverstone failure as F1 breaks before Spa
items.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli scored no points at the British Grand Prix, finishing 16th after a late mechanical failure and a five-second penalty, with Mercedes accepting blame. Formula 1 now pauses before the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa on 17-19 July.

items.headline: A robotic spacecraft launches to grab and reboost NASA's ageing Swift telescope
items.summary: Katalyst Space's LINK servicer launched on 3 July aboard a Pegasus XL from Kwajalein Atoll to rendezvous with the 21-year-old Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory and raise its decaying orbit, staving off an uncontrolled reentry expected by year's end. If it succeeds, it will be the first commercial craft to dock with a government satellite not built for servicing.

items.headline: Scientists record single neurons assembling sentences word by word before speech
items.summary: Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital paired recordings from individual neurons in the human frontotemporal cortex with AI language models, identifying cells that encode word meaning, grammar and sentence structure in the moment before a person speaks. The work appeared in Nature.

items.headline: NASA's TESS spots a giant planet 40,000 light-years away using a new method
items.summary: Astronomers confirmed Gaia23bra b, a planet about 1.6 times Jupiter's mass roughly 40,000 light-years away, far beyond TESS's usual 150-light-year reach, by using microlensing rather than its standard transit method. The find suggests other such planets are hiding in TESS data.

items.headline: Scientists race to save coffee as climate change threatens its wild species
items.summary: A Nature feature details how heat-sensitive Arabica and dozens of the 130-plus wild coffee species are increasingly threatened by warming and deforestation, pushing researchers toward heat-tolerant relatives such as Coffea stenophylla that grow at temperatures around 6°C higher.

fun_fact.headline: The inventor of the Pringles can was buried in one.
fun_fact.body: Fredric Baur, the organic chemist who designed the Pringles tubular can in the 1960s, was so proud of the invention that he asked to be buried in one. When he died in 2008 at age 89, his family honoured the request, placing part of his cremated remains inside an original Pringles can before burial in Ohio.

puzzle.title: The Tumbling Die
puzzle.body:
A standard die rests on a table. Opposite faces sum to 7.
Right now the 1 is face-up, the 2 faces toward you, and the 3 faces to your right.
You tip the die over its bottom edges through this sequence of quarter-rolls:

  right  →  away from you  →  left  →  away from you

Which number is face-up after the fourth roll?
puzzle.approach: Track the top face through each quarter-turn. Opposite faces always sum to 7, so once you know the top you know the bottom.
puzzle.answer:
3.

Start: top 1, toward-you 2, right 3 (so away 5, left 4, bottom 6).
Roll RIGHT  → top 4  (toward 2, away 5, right 1, left 6, bottom 3)
Roll AWAY   → top 2  (toward 3, away 4, right 1, left 6, bottom 5)
Roll LEFT   → top 1  (toward 3, away 4, right 5, left 2, bottom 6)
Roll AWAY   → top 3  (toward 6, away 1, right 5, left 2, bottom 4)

The die shows 3 on top.

word_puzzle.title: Crossed Wires
word_puzzle.body:
Sort these 16 words into four hidden groups of four:

GALAXY · IRON · WEDGE · MARS
SNICKERS · MERCURY · LEAD · DRIVER
TIN · BOUNTY · JUPITER · PUTTER
WOOD · SATURN · TWIX · ZINC
word_puzzle.approach: Sort the 16 words into four groups of four. Watch the overlaps — some words look like they belong to a tastier or more cosmic group than they really do.
word_puzzle.answer:
Planets: MARS · MERCURY · JUPITER · SATURN
Chocolate bars: GALAXY · SNICKERS · BOUNTY · TWIX
Metals (elements): IRON · LEAD · TIN · ZINC
Golf clubs: WEDGE · DRIVER · PUTTER · WOOD

Traps: GALAXY looks cosmic but is a chocolate bar; MARS looks like a chocolate bar but is the planet; MERCURY (element or planet) is a planet here; IRON (element or golf club) is an element.
